perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s perspective, the available information is:

- He is Keith Ndiaye, an African American man, a construction worker with a bachelor’s degree.
- He works with Elizabeth Sun, the receptionist, at the same construction company. Their relationship has been friendly but professional, mainly through his visits to the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, he noticed Elizabeth was unusually curt/short with him.
- He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She told him no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. She accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith perceived them as serious enough that professional help might benefit her.
- He suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. She said she had thought about it but was hesitant about seeking help.
- After this, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her. She said he had not overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of his concern.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. She thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith now believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him, and he intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
- He has no access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts, unspoken issues, or details of her stress beyond what she told him in conversation.
